standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: Reproductive planning: whether, when & spacing children; fertility awareness; preconception health; infertility & options (UNESCO 8.1, 6.2, 6.3). New v2 build, the reproductive-decision heart of Chapter 7 and the adult version of My Choices (g29). Whether to have children, when, and how many, made with real knowledge, together, and free of pressure in any direction. Six modes: whether & why (children are an if/when/whether choice, not the assumed default; childfree is a complete, valid life; bust 'a woman who doesn't want kids is selfish'), fertility for real (honest, calm fertility awareness, the fertile window, age trends for women AND men, preconception health and folic acid; bust both 'there's always time' and 'it just happens instantly', and refuse scare tactics), when & spacing (timing, readiness as honest reflection not perfection, spacing and contraception for spacing, your own timeline not the crowd's), if it's hard (infertility with compassion and realism, about 1 in 6 people, men and women roughly equally, options like IVF that help many but aren't guaranteed, no false hope and no shame; routes to Many Ways to Family g60), free of pressure (the couple's autonomy, resisting 'good news' and family pressure, confronting son-preference and sex-selection which are illegal under the PCPNDT Act, and refusing a weaponised fertility clock), tools & help (a decision-reflection tool, fertility basics, RKSK/public services and clinicians). Even-handed and non-coercive: no pressure toward children or against; childfree and many-paths-to-parenthood equally valid; medically accurate but panic-free; not medical advice, points to clinicians. Builds on My Choices (g29); pairs with Many Ways to Family (g60). India: intense family and social pressure to have children soon and ideally a son, infertility heavily stigmatised especially for women though male factor is common, sex selection illegal (PCPNDT Act), with support via RKSK and public reproductive-health services.

evidenceBase: Whether to have children, when, and how many is a genuine personal choice, not a foregone conclusion, and the node applies no pressure in any direction: a childfree life is complete and valid, womanhood is not the same as motherhood, and 'a woman who doesn't want children is selfish' is a myth to retire, while those who do want children are equally supported. Readiness is honest reflection on the essentials rather than waiting for everything to be perfect, timing and spacing are the couple's to set and revisit, and the decision belongs to the people who will live it, not to family or social expectation (UNESCO ITGSE autonomy & decision-making; childfree-by-choice and reproductive-autonomy research)

Honest fertility awareness is a calm planning tool, never a scare tactic: fertility declines gradually with age, sooner and faster for women (notably after the mid-30s) and somewhat for men too, conception can take several months even when all is well and is not instant on demand, and preconception health matters, with folic acid before and in early pregnancy sharply reducing certain birth defects such as neural tube defects. The framing refuses panic and 'fertility clock' weaponisation, presents facts so people can plan on their own terms, and treats fertility as a both-partners matter rather than only a woman's concern (WHO fertility and preconception guidance; age-and-fertility and folic-acid evidence)

Infertility is common and no one's shame, and the choice is protected from coercion: infertility affects around 1 in 6 people worldwide and involves men and women roughly equally, with male factors in about a third or more of cases, so both partners should be evaluated; treatments such as IVF help many but are not guaranteed and can be demanding, and family is whole in many forms, with adoption and other routes covered in Many Ways to Family (g60). Son-preference is unjust and prenatal sex determination and sex selection are illegal in India under the PCPNDT Act 1994, the node confronts 'good news' and son pressure, and it is general information rather than medical advice, pointing to clinicians and public services such as RKSK (WHO infertility 2023; PCPNDT Act 1994; MoHFW/RKSK reproductive-health services)

scenarios.hook: "There's no real way to make this choice well; you just hope it works out."
scenarios.relearn: You can make this choice well using honest reflection, accurate facts, partnership and freedom from pressure.

myth.un: There's no real way to make this choice well; you just hope it works out.
myth.re: You can make it well, with honest reflection, accurate facts, partnership and freedom from pressure.
myth.why: Big choices are navigable with the right tools.

scenarios.hook: A friend confides she's not sure she ever wants kids and feels guilty about it. You want to reassure her.
scenarios.relearn: Affirming that childfree is valid, with no 'you'll change your mind', lets her decide free of guilt.

yourLine.text: "That's a completely valid choice, you don't owe anyone children to live a full life."
"You'll change your mind, everyone does."

scenarios.hook: Your partner brushes off learning any fertility basics as 'her department'. You want to make it shared.
scenarios.relearn: Framing fertility as a both-of-us thing corrects the 'her department' default and shares the planning.

yourLine.text: "Fertility's a both-of-us thing, let's learn the basics together so we plan well."
"Yeah, that's really more your area."

scenarios.hook: An influencer post has you panicking that you've 'left it too late' at 33.
scenarios.relearn: Get calm, personal facts from a clinician; don't let a scare post rush a huge decision.

options.text: Step back and get calm, individual facts from a clinician
options.consequence: You replace panic with real information.

options.text: Spiral and make a rushed decision from fear
options.consequence: Calm individual facts from a clinician replace panic; a fear-driven rush makes a huge decision badly.

scenarios.debrief: Replace fertility panic with calm, individual facts from a clinician, not a rushed fear-decision.

scenarios.hook: Relatives keep asking when the 'second one' is coming. You want a light, firm reply.
scenarios.relearn: A light 'if and when, on what's right for us' holds your timing without conflict.

yourLine.text: "We'll decide if and when, on what's right for us, thanks for the love."
"Soon, I suppose, whenever they want."

scenarios.hook: Sort: a healthy input into timing, or pressure to ignore?
scenarios.relearn: Your readiness, health and partner's view are healthy inputs; imposed deadlines and competition are pressure.

items.text: A festival 'auspicious' deadline imposed on you

scenarios.hook: Match each 'when' question to who it really belongs to.
scenarios.relearn: Readiness, spacing and family size all belong to the couple, informed by health, not to relatives.

scenarios.hook: Your partner feels like 'a failure' after a hard fertility result. You want to hold them.
scenarios.relearn: Naming that it's not a failure and not theirs alone holds your partner and keeps you a team.

yourLine.text: "This isn't a failure and it isn't yours to carry alone, we face it together, with help."
"Maybe we just weren't meant to."

scenarios.hook: Treatment hasn't worked and you're exhausted, unsure whether to continue.
scenarios.relearn: Allow grief and honest counsel; continuing or stopping treatment is a caring choice, not 'giving up'.

options.text: Make space to grieve, get honest counsel, and choose your next step without shame
options.consequence: You decide from care, not pressure or false hope.

options.text: Push on endlessly because stopping feels like 'giving up'
options.consequence: Grief, honest counsel and a shame-free choice let you decide with care; endless pushing from 'never give up' can harm you.

scenarios.debrief: When treatment is hard, allow grief and honest counsel and choose your next step without shame.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a compassionate truth to hold onto, or a cruel myth to drop?
scenarios.relearn: 'Common, not your fault' and 'family takes many forms' are truths to hold; punishment and 'less of a person' are cruel myths.

items.text: Infertility is common and not your fault
Family can take many whole forms
You're 'less of a man or woman'

scenarios.hook: An elder insists you 'must give the family an heir, ideally a son'. You want to answer with calm dignity.
scenarios.relearn: A calm 'any child equally, ours to decide' rejects son-preference and holds your autonomy at once.

yourLine.text: "We'll welcome any child equally, and whether and when is ours to decide."
"We'll keep trying for a boy then."

scenarios.hook: You're offered an illegal test to reveal the baby's sex, with hints to 'plan accordingly'.
scenarios.relearn: Refuse illegal sex determination and selection; the law and justice both forbid it.

options.text: Refuse it firmly; sex determination and selection are illegal and unjust
options.consequence: You protect a daughter and obey the law.

options.text: Go along quietly to keep the peace
options.consequence: Refusing protects against sex selection and obeys the law; going along enables an illegal, unjust harm.

scenarios.debrief: Refuse prenatal sex determination and selection; they're illegal under the PCPNDT Act and deeply unjust.

scenarios.hook: Match each form of pressure to what actually counters it.
scenarios.relearn: Son-preference, nagging and a weaponised clock are each countered by equality, calm boundaries and your own timeline.

scenarios.hook: Spot the response that keeps the choice yours.
scenarios.relearn: Keep the choice yours: hold your timeline and refuse son-preference, don't conceive on demand.

scene.text: Holding your timeline kindly but firmly
Conceiving on demand to silence relatives
Refusing son-preference outright

scenarios.why: Holding your timeline and refusing son-preference keep the choice yours; conceiving on demand surrenders it.

scenarios.hook: You want to agree with your partner how you'll handle all the outside pressure together.
scenarios.relearn: A shared front, one calm line and leaning on each other keeps the pressure from splitting you.

yourLine.text: "Let's keep our decision between us, give everyone the same calm line, and lean on each other."
"Let's just tell people whatever they want to hear."

scenarios.hook: A worried younger relative asks you how to even start thinking about all this. You want to guide simply.
scenarios.relearn: A simple 'your wants, honest facts, your choice, no rush' hands her the calm method, not the pressure.

yourLine.text: "Start with what you want, get honest facts, and remember it's your choice, no rush."
"Just do what the family expects."

scenarios.hook: Sort: a trustworthy source for this decision, or one to be wary of?
scenarios.relearn: A clinician and public services like RKSK are trustworthy; 'guaranteed baby' clinics and scare media aren't.
